# Create Agent

A sub-agent starts fresh: it sees none of the parent conversation, and
the parent only receives its final report. This meta-skill guides the
content; `agentsdir add agent` guarantees the frontmatter Claude Code
requires. Six steps, in order.

## 1. Inventory before creating

- Read `.agents/agents/` first: an overlapping agent is improved, never
  duplicated. Keep the cumulated descriptions short — they share one
  context budget in the parent.

## 2. Targeted interview

- The bank is in references/interview.md. The anchor question: which
  SINGLE task, and how does the agent know it is finished?

## 3. Routing

- A sub-agent earns its place when the work is bulky or specialized AND
  isolable. Advisory knowledge is a rule ($create-rule); an on-demand
  workflow the main agent runs itself is a skill ($create-skill);
  something guaranteed on every event is a hook ($create-hook).

## 4. Draft, then critique

- Draft the system prompt: single mission, the REQUIRED output format
  (the parent receives only the report), and the boundaries. The prompt
  must never assume access to the parent conversation.
- Choose minimal tools (a reviewer has no Write or Edit) and a motivated
  model: mechanical volume → a fast model; deep reasoning → a strong
  one; otherwise inherit.
- Third-person description stating WHEN to delegate; add "use
  proactively" only when spontaneous delegation is wanted.
- Criticize every line with the filter
  question: "if this line is deleted, will the agent make a mistake?"
  Check against references/rubrique.md.

## 5. Generate, then write

- Run `agentsdir add agent <name> [--model <model>]`, then replace the
  template prompt with the drafted mission, output format and
  boundaries, and set the description from the interview.

## 6. Mechanical validation — mandatory

- Run `agentsdir check`. Any deviation goes back to step 4.
